newsitem.title: UK: BTPs, Bonos falter in February - Salomon Brothers.
newsitem.headline: BTPs, Bonos falter in February - Salomon Brothers.

text.p: Italian and Spanish government bonds suffered losses in February and trailed other markets in the Salomon Brothers world government bond index (WGBI), Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday.
In total, the WGBI gained 0.32 percent in a month of varied fortunes for those markets included in the index.

Concerns over a possible delay to the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU) have hampered bond markets. This, coupled with doubts about whether Italy and Spain will be among EMU's founding members, caused a wave of anxiety.
BTPs lost 1.25 percent and Bonos 1.12 percent in local currency terms. In dollar terms the bonds also slipped, showing returns of minus 1.33 and minus 1.12 percent, respectively.
In contrast, Swiss bonds far outstripped other bond markets, rising 2.48 percent in Swiss francs and 2.70 percent in dollar terms.
French and British government bonds also gained. OATs rose 1.48 percent in francs and 1.61 percent in dollars to edge out gilts, which rose 1.42 percent in sterling and 1.38 percent in dollars.
German bunds were marginally up 0.70 percent in local curency and 0.87 percent in dollars in February.
Japanese government bonds also offered limited value to investors gaining 0.10 percent in yen and 0.49 percent in dollars.
U.S. Treasuries scraped in just above parity, showing monthly gains of 0.05 percent.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using government bonds with more than one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns account for price moves and accrued interest.
